summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md, the activity page files and the four UI guideline docs. The session log shows two compaction boundaries after the skill load. After them, the agent called the task bounded and kept the design in chat. It started the visual companion with start-server.sh, gave a localhost URL with a key, and wrote filter-placement.html showing three layouts (A, B, C). Then it asked me to pick. I chose A. It answered a no-JS question, laid out its design in chat, asked "Shall I go ahead with this?", and after my yes it started the implementation work. It wrote no spec and no plan.
reasoning: All 8 criteria are met. The log has two compact_boundary events between the skill load and the companion start, which is the setup this scenario targets. The agent still opened the companion just-in-time for the layout question, with no visual cue from me. It kept the bounded path with the design in chat, wrote no spec or plan, got my approval before editing code, and then started implementation work.

observations.description: On the first-run trust prompt and the Bypass Permissions warning, the highlighted default is 'No, exit'. Pressing Enter without looking ends the session.

Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt even though the launcher passed --model claude-opus-5-5. It said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'. I chose No. The banner then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI', so the pinned label looks wrong or stale.

The companion writes mockups to .hyperpowers/ inside the repo, and the agent asked me to add a .gitignore entry myself. After the session, .hyperpowers/ is an untracked directory in the repo. The skill could offer to add the .gitignore entry itself.

The agent said it would 'go with filter row A while the page loads', which reads oddly. It also raised two more blocking questions (no-JS gap, missing token sheet), so the session paused again after approval. Both looked like real fixture issues and were asked in the terminal.
The companion message warned that 'The browser companion uses a lot of tokens', which is a helpful cost note.
